observations.behavior: Adds a size check and helper to prevent oversized JSON schemas from being passed to an LLM judge.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks the character count of serialized query models before use; this could avoid token limits or degraded performance in evaluation. No score is assigned.

observations.behavior: Changes group type mapping clearing behavior: when no PersonHog client exists, it now invalidates cached mappings instead of proceeding without one.
observations.posthog_connection: This could preserve cache consistency for dashboards that rely on PersonHog as their only store. The change also adds a test covering unconfigured clients.

observations.behavior: Replaces direct schema dictionary with model-based serialization using shared references rather than inline definitions.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces payload size while retaining compatibility with existing scoring expectations. This could help keep evaluations within context windows.

observations.limitations: The hunks are spread across several unrelated modules (evaluation scorers, group-type-mapping cleanup) and do not share a single coherent goal. One hunk removes unused imports, another changes caching behavior, and others adjust how query models are supplied to evaluators. Without release notes or metadata linking these together, we cannot establish whether they form a coordinated improvement or independent maintenance work. No tier can be defended; the grouping itself lacks sufficient evidence of benefit.

review.reason: Grouping issue: this chunk mixes three distinct concerns—LLM evaluation input preparation, database-cache handling, and minor import cleanup. None demonstrate systemic risk reduction or broader capability. Tier 2 requires bounded implementation and checks visible in the same logical unit; here each piece is narrow and isolated. Tier 3 requires cross-component demonstration absent from this patch. No score assigned.
review.posthog_relevance: Changes could support reliability and performance but lack demonstrated reach. The cache invalidation might prevent stale dashboard mappings if PersonHog is unavailable; the JSON-schema helper could avoid token overruns during automated insight generation. However, no adoption or incident avoidance is shown.
review.abstention_reason: This chunk does not represent a conservatively grouped change with shared benefit. It combines unrelated hunks across different subsystems without clear dependency or common outcome. A single hunk alone would warrant at most a 1, while the whole group cannot earn higher tiers.
